00255 /**

00258  *
00259  * Applications cannot override the OnButtonDown callback for certain compound
00260  * widgets (HxFileList_t and HxStorageList_t), because the event is passed
00261  * to underlying components.
00262  *
00263  * If the application implements a button down callback for an HxContainer_t, 
00264  * use the kHxContainerAttrKeepEvents flag to avoid having the motion event
00265  * passed to the container's children.
00266  *
00267  * In general, applications should use HxListenToMessage, defined in 
00268  * hxmessage.h, to listen for the button "action" message.  Alternatively, 
00269  * to target a specific widget rather than all widgets of a particular type, 
00270  * use HxWidgetMapMessageCallback.  For example, listen for 
00271  * kHxCommandButtonChanged for command button selection, kHxCheckboxChanged
00272  * for a checkbox toggle, or kHxGadgetSelected for a button down and up
00273  * within a gadget.
00274  **/
00275 typedef int32_t (*HxWidgetOnButtonDownFnPtr)(HxWidget_t* pWidget,
00276                                         int32_t x, int32_t y,
00277                                         HxMouseButton_t button);

00404 /**
00405  * @brief               Set (and get) a widget's callback
00406  *
00407  * Widget callbacks are called by the system in response to events.
00408  * For example, command buttons have callbacks for button down, button
00409  * up, and key down events.  This function makes it possible for the
00410  * application to override a widget's callbacks.
00411  *
00412  * pCallback can be set to NULL if the caller only wants hOldCallback
00413  * returned.
00414  *
00415  * If hOldCallback is not NULL, the old callback is returned.  Normally, an
00416  * application should call the default system callback after performing
00417  * its custom operation.  For example, the application can use this
00418  * function to save the default Draw callback, calling it after performing
00419  * any custom drawing in its widget.
00420  *
00421  * Normally, a pointer to an HxWindow_t structure should never be passed to
00422  * an HxWidget API.  It is appropriate, however, for applications to override
00423  * the certain callbacks.  HX_INVALID_ARG is returned, however, if a window
00424  * is passed to this function for the following widget-specific callbacks:
00425  *
00426  *      kHxWidgetFocusStateChange
00427  *      kHxWidgetEnabledStateChange
00428  *      kHxWidgetVisibleStateChange
00429  *      kHxWidgetResize
00430  *      kHxWidgetDirectFocus
00431  *
00432  * @param pWidget       IN:     Pointer to the widget
00433  * @param selector      IN:     Callback selector
00434  * @param pCallback     IN:     Pointer to a widget's callback, or NULL
00435  * @param hCallback     OUT:    Handle to a widget's old callback, or NULL
00436  *
00437  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK on success.
00438  *
00439  **/
00440 HxResult HxWidgetSetCallback(HxWidget_t* pWidget,
00441                                     HxCallbackSelector_t selector,
00442                                     void* pCallback, void** hOldCallback);
00443

00462 /**
00463  * @brief               
00464  *
00465  * A message callbacks is the normal way an application reacts to user actions.
00466  * This is the recommended way to respond to events, rather than using the
00467  * HxWidgetSetCallback API, which replaces the low-level event handler.
00468  *
00469  * This function associates a message callback with a particular message
00470  * action, such as a command button press or a double click in a list.
00471  *
00472  * If pWidget is NULL, then the callback is called for any message
00473  * sender.  If pWidget is not NULL, the callback is only called when
00474  * that widget is the sender of the message. 
00475  *
00476  * messageClass would be set to kHxActionMessageClass for messages associated
00477  * with widgets, or set to kHxInputMessageClass for input messages from the
00478  * keyboard, mouse, or scroll wheel.
00479  *
00480  * messageAction would be set to the type of message for which the application
00481  * is listening (i.e., kHxCheckboxChanged). See messagedomain.h for a full
00482  * listing.
00483  *
00484  * An application can associate more than one messageAction and
00485  * callback with a widget.  Messages associated with a widget will be
00486  * unregistered by the system when the widget is destroyed.
00487  *
00488  * If pCallback is NULL, the callback for the message action associated with
00489  * the widget is removed.  Note that this should not be done for broadcasted
00490  * messages.
00491  *
00492  * HX_INVALID_ARG is returned if pWidget is a pointer to a HxWindow_t.  If
00493  * an application wants to listen to input events for a window, use 
00494  * HxWindowSetHandler (see hxwindow.h) or HxMessageListen (see hxmessage.h).
00495  *
00496  *
00497  * @param pWidget       IN:     Pointer to a widget
00498  * @param messageClass  IN:     Message class (kHxActionMessageClass or
00499  *                              kHxInputMessageClass)
00500  * @param messageAction IN:     Type of message
00501  * @param pCallback     IN:     Callback function, or NULL
00502  * @param pData         IN:     Pointer to user data, or NULL
00503  *
00504  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00505  *                              Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if messageAction is
00506  *                              not valid.
00507  *
00508  **/
00509 HxResult HxWidgetMapMessageCallback(HxWidget_t* pWidget,
00510                                     int32_t messageClass, int32_t messageAction,
00511                                     HxMessageCallback pCallback, void* pData);
00512

01044  * missing widgets will no longer be capable of receiving focus for purposes

01048  * navigation for the topmost visible window.  If idCount is 0, then pIdArray
01049  * can be NULL.  Use HxWindowSetFocusArray to clear the focus array for a
01050  * window other than the topmost visible window.

01053  * are appended to the focus array.
